text:
maria: quick follow-up to the RFC re: unifying credential types. goal is smaller public surface and easier revocation/migration. link: https://rfc/redwood/cred-unify

devin: read it. sounds good. what's the minimal compatibility story for existing project API keys? we have dozens in-huge customers

maria: plan A: auth service will accept legacy project-key and return a short-lived scoped token on first use. we add Deprecation header to responses so clients see timeline

sam: ok but how do we represent permissions? today keys carry role bindings per project. if we move to identity-first model we need clear RBAC mapping rules

ben: thought: keep a canonical principal id for each key. migration maps legacy_key -> canonical_principal -> new identity-key. RBAC stays attached to canonical_principal, so no semantics change during rollout

zoe: that helps telemetry too. billing and per-key metrics can use canonical_principal as the single source of truth

devin: token exchange could be per-request overhead. we should allow server-side caching of exchanged session tokens for a short TTL keyed by (caller_key, requested_scope)

msam: runtime concern: KV/prefix cache entries must be tied to token id so that if a session is revoked we can evict entries. runtime already supports eviction by principal id but token-level is new

maria: agree. we'll extend runtime cache tags to include session_id field. revocation stream will publish both canonical_principal and session ids for immediate eviction

ben: delegation and cross-org use cases? do we permit org-level long-lived keys or require explicit delegation tokens signed by the delegator org

zoe: prefer signed delegation objects (broker pattern). example from notes: ```{
  from: org:acme,
  to: svc:partner-app,
  allowed: ["inference:invoke", "embeddings:read"],
  expiry: 1700000000,
  sig: <base64sig>
}```

maria: this reduces blast radius vs org-wide global keys. delegation objects are minted by auth service and can be validated by runtimes without extra lookups

devin: how about operator workflows (cron jobs, db migrations) that need long-lived non-interactive creds? we can't break them overnight

maria: we'll keep a long-lived "issuer" credential for operator use but require rotation policy and encourage using identity-keys backed by KMS/HSM for private deployments. hosted tenants get recommended short TTLs by default

ben: revocation semantics: we get near-instant block for identity-keys (revoke canonical_principal) and for session tokens we rely on revocation stream + blacklist. need to measure latency to enforcement at edge nodes

zoe: I'll run a small spike to measure average revocation propagation time and cache eviction overhead across zones. volunteer to own that spike

sam: migration tooling? we need a bulk tool: scan old keys, create identity-keys, and optionally rotate clients using a shadow-issuance mode so traffic continues during cutover

maria: yes. plan: (1) compatibility shim that mints session tokens and sends Deprecation header, (2) canonical_principal mapping in auth DB, (3) migration cli for bulk conversion + rotation, (4) runtime cache tagging + revocation hookup, (5) docs and deprecation timeline

infra-bot: Merge check: "cred-unify-compat-shim" PR opened. CI: unit + lint pass, e2e migration tests queued

ben: small policy Q: when session token inherits permissions do we take union or intersection of requested scope vs identity grants? I think intersection (deny by default)

maria: correct: session grants = intersection(requested_scopes, identity_grants) and delegation object further narrows it. explicit deny logic will remain enforced at policy layer

zoe: noted. I'll update the RFC appendix with the canonical_principal field and mapping examples.

devin: I'll pair with Zoe on the revocation spike tomorrow. scheduling drop-in

sam: :+1:

maria: thanks everyone. I'll add a rollout checklist and target a 6-week migration window with opt-in early adopters first :calendar:

zoe: thumbs up :rocket:
